problem: Almost all VLN agents are discriminative (follower-style) policies that directly predict p(a|X,h), which overfit to seen environments. Speaker models are used only for data augmentation or reranking whole trajectories, never as a standalone step-wise policy.
motivation: Generating the entire instruction given an action gives a richer learning signal than predicting a single action label. This should make the policy more sensitive to the language and more robust in unseen environments, as generative classifiers (naive Bayes) versus discriminative ones (logistic regression) suggest. The generative form also allows token-level interpretability.
key_idea: Use a language model p(X|a_t,h_t) conditioned on each candidate action and the history, and apply Bayes' rule with a uniform action prior to obtain the policy, choosing argmax_a p(X|a,h).
insight: The generative policy beats the discriminative policy with identical architecture and augmentation in R2R val-unseen (SR 0.476 vs 0.431), and has more tolerance to accumulated error at later steps (action precision plot). It follows the reference path more closely (higher CLS/nDTW/SDTW). Combining the generative and discriminative policies gives the best results, and their action agreement drops over time, so they capture different aspects. Without augmentation the discriminative policy overfits seen environments, while the generative one is better on unseen.
method: Generative policy via Bayes' rule: p(a|X,h)=p(X|a,h)/sum_a' p(X|a',h) with uniform prior; act by argmax over candidate actions of the instruction likelihood.
Training objective: maximize log p(X|a_t*,h_t) minus log sum over all actions of p(X|a',h_t), i.e. a language-model term plus a term penalizing all actions; both terms are needed.

Architecture: speaker network of Speaker-Follower (panoramic view, action embedding of orientation [sin,cos of heading/elevation] plus ResNet feature) as the language model; the follower architecture is used for the discriminative baseline.

Training regime: pretrain the language model on trajectory-to-instruction, then fine-tune with a teacher/student-forcing mixture (eta=1/3); R2R uses the 178K augmented data then original; R4R uses supervised or fidelity-oriented heuristics.
Gen+Disc combination: argmax of beta*log p(X|a,h)+(1-beta)*log p_f(a|X,h) with beta=0.5, optionally with FAST-style backtracking.
TENT (token-wise prediction entropy): normalized entropy over actions of each token's likelihood, visualized as 1-TENT to show which tokens drive action decisions.

setting.backbone: Speaker-Follower-style LSTM language model (generative) and follower network (discriminative), with ResNet image features, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: R2R train (14,025 instructions) plus 178.3K augmented trajectories from Speaker-Follower; R4R train (233k instructions) without augmentation
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ResNet features) with heading/elevation orientation features
setting.privileged: none (single-run, no beam search, no pre-exploration)

numbers.extra: trained with 178K augmented data; single run, no beam search

numbers.evidence: Table 1, Gen.+Disc.(A+B)* unseen; * = backtracking of FAST

numbers_note: Metrics printed as fractions were converted to percent, and the quote fragments in evidence keep the printed form. R4R seen results are also reported but not listed here.
results: On R2R val-unseen the generative policy (SR 0.476, SPL 0.405) beats the same-architecture discriminative policy with augmentation (SR 0.431, SPL 0.392). The Gen+Disc combination with backtracking reaches test-unseen SR 0.54 / SPL 0.46, matching FAST in SR and near EnvDrop (0.47) in SPL. On R4R val-unseen the generative policy beats the discriminative one, and supervised Gen has the best CLS (0.479) among baselines, though BabyWalk still has better SDTW.
limitations: Computing the posterior requires evaluating the language model for every candidate action, which may not scale to large action sets; the authors suggest importance sampling or amortized inference.

Does not use RL, curriculum, or large-scale pretraining, and on R4R without augmentation the discriminative policy is sometimes as good or better on seen environments; BabyWalk remains better in SDTW.
